headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks; no direct shared channel, but dbt can consume ComfyUI outputs if wired together.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline-capable and has no clipboard/MCP surface, while dbt-core exposes only allowlisted warehouse/API egress. No default shared channel is documented, so prompt injection is not inherent. If an operator manually pipes ComfyUI text outputs into dbt macros or docs, injected instructions could propagate, but that requires unusual setup.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies ComfyUI-generated text into dbt macros, docs, or SQL comments
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added between the agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable any manual copy-paste bridge for generated text
Review dbt inputs for untrusted prose before execution
Use a human approval step for any text imported from ComfyUI

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts locally, and dbt-core touches warehouse data via allowlisted egress. The profiles do not show a shared filesystem or common OAuth principal, so leakage is not default. If the operator connects ComfyUI outputs to warehouse-backed dbt inputs, sensitive data could cross systems, but that is configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are exported into a warehouse table consumed by dbt
IF both agents are granted access to the same shared directory containing sensitive assets
mitigations: Store ComfyUI artifacts in a separate directory
Restrict dbt sources to non-sensitive schemas
Audit any export/import job between the tools
Mask or redact sensitive fields before transfer

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and dbt-core exposes no write-capability surface in the profile beyond warehouse/API access. With no overlapping mutable local resource or locking issue shown, a direct capability conflict is not plausible from the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to grant both agents write access to the same directory
IF dbt-core is configured with mutable git or filesystem writes
mitigations: Keep local writes disabled for ComfyUI
Avoid shared mutable directories
Run dbt in a separate service account
Add explicit locking if a shared resource is introduced

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can generate workflows and artifacts that a downstream operator may treat as authoritative, while dbt-core can act on warehouse data through API calls. The pair lacks a documented verification boundary, so if ComfyUI output is fed into dbt models or docs without review, errors can cascade into incorrect transformations or published analytics. This is inferred from the profiles, not directly observed.
conditions: IF dbt models or docs are generated from ComfyUI output without human review
IF ComfyUI-produced artifacts are used as source-of-truth inputs for warehouse transformations
mitigations: Require review before dbt execution
Tag ComfyUI outputs as untrusted
Add schema checks on imported text or metadata
Separate generation from deployment steps

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI is open-source, offline-capable, and touches local media/model artifacts; dbt-core interacts with warehouse data and allowlisted egress. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented in the profiles, so compliance risk is limited to operator-managed data flows. The other agent is not cited separately because no specific cross-border or regulated-data pathway is shown.
conditions: IF regulated data from the warehouse is exported into ComfyUI artifacts
IF the warehouse contains data subject to stricter retention than the local ComfyUI workspace
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ComfyUI inputs
Document retention for exported artifacts
Use separate storage for warehouse extracts
Review residency requirements before any export
